title: RootSeqCache saturation holds new roots at unsigned Baseline indefinitely (residual of r2oz fix)
description: Residual design risk noted in r2oz security review, NOT introduced by that fix: a persistent on-link adversary who keeps the 16-entry RootSeqCache (lichen-rpl/src/root_seq_cache.rs MAX_ROOT_SEQ_KEYS) saturated holds every NEW genuine DODAG's signed DIOs at Baseline indefinitely, so per-root signed replay tracking never engages for them. Pre-r2oz this was a hard DoS; post-r2oz it is parity with unsigned-DIO processing (which the adversary could emit anyway), so no guarantee is weakened — but the 0x17 anti-replay guarantee never activates for new roots under sustained saturation. Candidate mitigations (design tradeoff, needs spec input): larger table, eviction by verification recency/preference, operator-visible saturation metric, or persistent high-water marks (intersects eebl's storage work). File under spec 06 8.10.1 hardening.
